subject: Energy
title: Energy in the Food Chain
description: Learn Energy in the Food Chain in one minute.

hook.text: Energy flows through ecosystems—from sunlight to plants to herbivores to predators, shrinking at every step.

buildup.text: At each level, about 90% of energy is lost as heat—only 10% passes to the next consumer.

discovery.text: That's why ecosystems have far fewer predators than prey—there's not enough energy to support many top predators.

twist.text: Eating grain directly is 10 times more energy-efficient than feeding it to cattle and eating the meat.

climax.text: A tuna sits 4–5 levels up the food chain—it takes roughly 10,000 kg of plankton to produce 1 kg of tuna.

punchline.text: Energy fades at each link—top predators live on scraps.

quiz.question: How much energy transfers between trophic levels?
